title: Catering, ii
logline: Thursday of the week the book keeps. The crab cakes, analyzed. Gully's girl, four, eats the drawing.

panels.composition: Gully's. WOOD on the stool with a pad: a diagram of a crab cake in cross-section, labeled. GULLY. The girl, four, on the counter. BARNABY in the basket on the counter.

balloons.text: Panko. Not breadcrumb. Panko. Three-to-one crab-to-binder, which is generous, which is the point —

image.prompt: a thin man on a shop stool drawing a labeled cross-section diagram of a crab cake, a man in an apron, a four-year-old girl sitting on the counter, an old dog in a basket on the counter, razor-sharp ink
close-up of a precise hand-drawn cross-section diagram of a crab cake with arrows and ratio annotations
image.notes: Labels unreadable except one: letter 'aioli (house)' after.

panels.composition: The girl taking the page. Folding it. Putting it in her mouth.

image.prompt: a four-year-old girl folding a drawing and putting it in her mouth while two men watch

panels.composition: Wood starting a new one. Gully's hand flat on the pad.

balloons.text: It was a good crab cake, Gully.

image.prompt: a stocky man pressing his hand flat on a thin man's drawing pad to stop him, an old dog in a basket between them

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: 'Draw the dog.' The girl eats the diagram.
